The four contracts represent a material revenue and backlog stream. The added representations allocate risk and create a clean basis for the covenants and conditions below.''',
'DD Memo §§VI.A–C; Playbook §12.2; Term Sheet §7 (government-contract representations)')

# Article VI
add_para(doc,'IV. ARTICLE VI — COVENANTS',style='Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,'7. Section 6.01(b) — restrict new, amended, extended or terminated affiliate transactions','HIGH',
'''Section 6.01(b) lists actions requiring Buyer consent, including indebtedness, capital expenditures, material contracts, personnel, litigation, Taxes, assets, liens and restrictive covenants, but contains no specific restriction on transactions with Seller or any Affiliate of Seller.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 6.01(b)(xiv):

“(xiv) enter into, amend, extend, renew, terminate, waive, or otherwise modify any contract, agreement, arrangement, or transaction with Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, including the Affiliate Lease, the Management Services Agreement, the Tax Sharing Agreement, or any other shared-services, occupancy, procurement, financing, or other affiliate arrangement, or make any payment or incur any obligation thereunder, in each case without Buyer’s prior written consent; provided that the Company may terminate the Management Services Agreement and the Tax Sharing Agreement at or prior to Closing in accordance with this Agreement.”''',
'''The existing disclosure of affiliate arrangements is not a substitute for an interim covenant. The affiliate lease carries $1.6M of annual rent and is relevant to Adjusted EBITDA; the seller should not be able to expand, amend, extend or terminate affiliate arrangements during the interim period without Buyer’s consent. This is an express Playbook checklist item.''',
'Playbook §3.2 and §14(2); DD Memo §VIII; Schedule 4.21')

add_issue(doc,'8. New Section 6.12 — government contract novation and recognition cooperation','CRITICAL',
'''Seller’s draft has only a general third-party-consent covenant: “Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain ... all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required ... including those set forth on Schedule 4.05.” It does not specifically address government-contract novation or FAR Part 42.''',
'''Add the following new Section 6.12:

“Section 6.12 Government Contract Novation and Recognition.

(a) Promptly after the date of this Agreement, Seller and the Company shall notify each applicable federal and state contracting officer of the transactions contemplated hereby and shall prepare and submit all requests, notices, novation packages, recognition requests, change-of-control notices, and other submissions required under applicable Law or the Government Contracts, including the novation requests required under FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12 for Contract No. W912DR-21-D-0045 with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Contract No. L23PX-00412 with the Bureau of Land Management.

(b) Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, before the Closing to the extent reasonably practicable, all required novation agreements, recognition agreements, consents, approvals, and written confirmations permitting continued performance under the Government Contracts. Seller shall provide Buyer copies of all submissions, communications, requests for information, and responses, and shall not make any material submission without giving Buyer a reasonable opportunity to review and comment.

(c) Seller and the Company shall not withdraw, amend, or abandon any submission and shall promptly notify Buyer of any denial, adverse determination, cure notice, termination notice, suspension notice, or indication that a Governmental Authority may terminate, suspend, not renew, or materially modify a Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated hereby.

(d) Following the Closing, Seller shall reasonably cooperate, at no material out-of-pocket cost to Seller, with Buyer and the Company in completing each novation, recognition, consent, approval, or change-of-control process, including executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers, until all such processes are finally resolved.”''',
'''A general consent clause is insufficient for federal government contracts. The DD Memo identifies the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR 42.12, with potential contract termination if required novations are not obtained. The recommended structure requires pre-Closing submission and best efforts but avoids making full agency completion an absolute condition given 60–120+ day agency timelines; it preserves a post-Closing cooperation tail. Partner/client should decide whether to elevate receipt of written “no denial/no termination” confirmations to a hard condition.''',
'DD Memo §VI; Playbook §12.2; Partner Instructions ¶4')

add_issue(doc,'9. New Section 6.13 — environmental permit change-of-control cooperation','MEDIUM',
'''The seller draft has a general Section 6.05 third-party-consent covenant but no covenant addressing the Company’s 23 environmental permits or change-of-control filings, notices, or approvals.''',
'''Add the following new Section 6.13:

“Section 6.13 Environmental Permit Notifications and Approvals.

(a) Before the Closing, Seller and the Company shall identify each Environmental Permit requiring notice to, consent or approval of, or other filing with any Governmental Authority as a result of the transactions contemplated hereby, including the Environmental Permits issued in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. Seller and the Company shall prepare and submit all required notices, applications, and requests for approval within the time required by applicable Law or the applicable Environmental Permit and shall provide Buyer copies promptly after submission.

(b) Seller and the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all required approvals and to confirm that the Company may continue operating under each Environmental Permit pending any agency review. Seller and the Company shall promptly notify Buyer of any agency objection, deficiency notice, threatened suspension, or other adverse communication.

(c) For twelve (12) months following the Closing, Seller shall reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the Company in completing any required notification, transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or approval process, including executing documents, supplying historical information, and participating in agency communications as reasonably requested by Buyer. This covenant shall continue beyond twelve (12) months to the extent necessary to complete a process timely commenced during that period.”''',
'''The stock structure does not eliminate change-of-control risk. The DD Memo identifies state-specific requirements in Oregon, Washington, California and Nevada and recommends both pre- and post-Closing cooperation for at least 12 months. This provision should be paired with the Section 7.02 closing protection below for permits requiring prior approval.''',
'DD Memo §V.B; Playbook §§12.1 and 13.2; Partner Instructions ¶10')

add_issue(doc,'10. Section 6.09 — narrow non-compete and conform non-solicitation period','MEDIUM',
'''(a) For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not ... engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States ...

(b) For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not ... solicit ... any employee ... or solicit or encourage ... any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship ...''',
'''Replace Sections 6.09(a) and 6.09(b) with:

“(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its controlled Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date, in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada; provided that this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) Seller’s or its Affiliates’ existing construction and timber operations, (ii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity, or (iii) environmental-related activities incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller’s construction or timber operations.

(b) Non-Solicitation. For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its controlled Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce, encourage, or attempt to induce or encourage any such employee to terminate employment with the Company; provided that this Section 6.09(b) shall not restrict general solicitations not specifically directed to Company employees or the hiring of an employee who contacts Seller or its Affiliates on the employee’s own initiative without solicitation.”''',
'''The current five-year, nationwide, “any business” prohibition is materially broader than the binding Term Sheet, would sweep in Seller’s construction and timber operations, and creates enforceability risk. The buyer markup tracks the agreed 3-year / four-state / business-scope limitations and uses the Term Sheet’s 2-year employee non-solicit. Customer/supplier non-solicitation is not included in the proposed language because it is not in the binding Term Sheet and the partner instructions direct exact conformity.''',
'Term Sheet §11 and §18(v); Playbook §10.1; Partner Instructions ¶12')

# Article VII
add_para(doc,'V. ARTICLE VII — CONDITIONS TO CLOSING',style='Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,'11. Section 7.02 — payoff letters and simultaneous payoff as express Buyer condition','HIGH',
'''Section 2.03(d): “At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.”

Section 7.02 contains no condition expressly requiring delivery of payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing.''',
'''Replace Section 2.03(d) with:

“(d) Repayment of Closing Indebtedness. At least three (3) Business Days before the Closing Date, Seller shall deliver to Buyer executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness, including Cascade Mutual Bank, Pacific Lease Corp., and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable indebtedness in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, and all other amounts, provide wire instructions, and provide for the release at Closing of all liens and other security interests securing such indebtedness, together with UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents. All Closing Indebtedness shall be paid simultaneously at the Closing through the funds flow, and no Closing Indebtedness shall remain outstanding after the Closing.”

Add the following as new Section 7.02(h):

“(h) Payoff Letters. Buyer shall have received, at least three (3) Business Days before the Closing Date, executed payoff letters satisfying Section 2.03(d) from each holder of Closing Indebtedness, and Seller shall have delivered all lien releases and termination documents required to be delivered at Closing under those payoff letters.”''',
'''“At or promptly following” Closing is insufficient for lender diligence and may leave liens or the $28M senior loan, $9.8M equipment financing, or $4.5M seller note outstanding. The Term Sheet requires payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing, simultaneous payoff through the closing funds flow, and a Buyer closing condition. The buyer may waive the condition or delay Closing, but should not be deemed to have waived it by proceeding absent an express written waiver.''',
'Term Sheet §6; Playbook §9.2; Partner Instructions ¶9')

add_issue(doc,'12. Section 7.02 — add government-contract and permit closing protections','CRITICAL',
'''Section 7.02(f) requires only that “[a]ll consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.” The draft does not require government-contract novation submissions/no denial, permit filings/approvals, or an environmental no-new-claims condition.''',
'''Add the following as new Sections 7.02(i) through (l):

“(i) Government Contract Submissions; No Adverse Action. All notices, novation requests, recognition requests, and other submissions required under Section 6.12 for the Government Contracts shall have been timely submitted, and no applicable contracting officer or Governmental Authority shall have denied such request or notified Seller, the Company, or Buyer of an intent to terminate, suspend, not renew, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated hereby. To the extent any applicable contracting officer has provided written confirmation that interim performance will be permitted pending final novation or recognition, Buyer shall have received such confirmation.

(j) Environmental Permit Notifications and Approvals. All notices required to be filed under Section 6.13 shall have been filed, and all prior approvals required under applicable Law or any Environmental Permit for the change of control shall have been obtained or waived in writing by the applicable Governmental Authority. No Governmental Authority shall have notified Seller or the Company that the Company may not continue operating under any material Environmental Permit after the Closing.

(k) No New Environmental Claims. Since the date of this Agreement, the Company shall not have received any new material environmental claim, enforcement action, notice of violation, CERCLA information request, or similar regulatory action that, individually or in the aggregate, would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

(l) Environmental Insurance. The environmental impairment liability insurance policy and the Hargrove Industrial Site project-specific environmental liability policy shall remain in full force and effect as of the Closing Date, with coverage limits no less than those in effect on the date of this Agreement, and no notice of cancellation, non-renewal, or material coverage limitation shall have been received.”''',
'''The seller draft’s generic Schedule 4.05 condition does not protect the four material Government Contracts or the 23-permit portfolio. The recommended condition is a balanced position: require submission and no adverse agency action, rather than absolute completion of all novations, because agency timing may exceed the Outside Date. The environmental no-new-claims and insurance conditions are required sector-specific protections under the Playbook.''',
'DD Memo §§V, VI and VII; Playbook §§12.1, 12.2, 13.1 and 13.2; Partner Instructions ¶4')

add_issue(doc,'13. Section 7.02 — add R&W Insurance policy condition','MEDIUM',
'''The seller draft contains no condition requiring evidence that Buyer’s representations and warranties insurance policy has been bound and is in full force and effect.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 7.02(m):

“(m) R&W Insurance. Buyer shall have received evidence reasonably satisfactory to Buyer that the representations and warranties insurance policy obtained by Buyer or its Affiliates in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby has been bound and is in full force and effect as of the Closing Date.”''',
'''The Term Sheet identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters and the Playbook treats a bound R&W policy as a standard Buyer closing condition when Buyer is obtaining R&W Insurance. The condition should not be subject to Seller approval or become a financing condition; it simply confirms the agreed risk-transfer structure.''',
'Term Sheet §10; Playbook §13.1(l) and §8.2')

# Article IX
add_para(doc,'VI. ARTICLE IX — INDEMNIFICATION',style='Heading 1')
add_issue(doc,'14. Section 9.01(b) — separate environmental representation survival','HIGH',
'''(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.''',
'''Replace Section 9.01(b) with:

“(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations and the Environmental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire, except with respect to claims properly asserted in accordance with Section 9.05 before expiration. The representations and warranties set forth in Section 4.15 (Environmental Matters), Section 4.16 (Government Contracts) to the extent relating to environmental or regulatory compliance, and Section 4.17 (Insurance) to the extent relating to environmental insurance (collectively, the ‘Environmental Representations’) shall survive the Closing for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, and any claim based on an Environmental Representation properly asserted in accordance with Section 9.05 before expiration shall survive until finally resolved. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival through the full applicable statute of limitations for environmental claims.”''',
'''The draft’s 12-month blanket survival conflicts with the Term Sheet’s 18-month general period and the Playbook’s 36-month minimum for environmental representations. Dalton Creek may not crystallize within 12 months, and Hargrove remediation continues 18–24+ months post-Closing. The opening position should be full applicable limitations period; the instructed drafting assumption is 36 months, with the longer alternative flagged for Marcus and the partner.''',

add_issue(doc,'15. New Section 9.02(e) — Dalton Creek Special Indemnity','CRITICAL',
'''Seller draft Section 9.02 covers breaches of representations, covenants, Transaction Expenses and Pre-Closing Taxes, but contains no special indemnity for the Dalton Creek disposal facility or the EPA CERCLA §104(e) information request.''',
'''Add the following as new Section 9.02(e), and add a corresponding Schedule 9.02(e) identifying the matter:

“(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the EPA information request under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility in Oregon, (ii) any investigation, inquiry, claim, notice of potential responsibility, designation as a potentially responsible party, enforcement action, administrative order, consent decree, lawsuit, contribution claim, or other proceeding relating to the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, and (iii) any contamination, release, threatened release, response cost, remediation obligation, natural resource damage, property damage, bodily injury, defense cost, settlement, judgment, penalty, fine, or other liability arising from or relating to the Company’s operations, transportation, arranging for disposal, or disposal of Hazardous Substances at or in connection with the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, whether arising under CERCLA, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Oregon Environmental Cleanup Law, or any other applicable Law. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall apply whether or not the applicable Loss constitutes a breach of any representation or warranty and shall include all reasonable attorneys’ fees, consultants’ fees, investigation costs, and costs of enforcing this Section 9.02(e).”

Schedule 9.02(e) — Scheduled Environmental Matter: Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, Oregon; EPA CERCLA §104(e) information request concerning former Company operations and waste disposal activities; estimated exposure $1,500,000–$6,000,000; regulatory reference number: none provided as of the date of this Agreement.”''',
'''This is a required deal term, not a minor drafting point. The Dalton Creek matter is a known, disclosed environmental liability with a $1.5M–$6M estimated range and a long-tail CERCLA risk. Because it is disclosed, it may not support a general rep claim; it therefore needs a standalone indemnity covering investigation, defense, remediation, response costs and enforcement, with no dependence on breach, schedule disclosure, or ultimate PRP designation.''',
'Term Sheet §9; Playbook §6; DD Memo §§III.A–C and VIII; Partner Instructions ¶7')

add_issue(doc,'16. Section 9.04 — cap, escrow and insurance mechanics','HIGH',
'''(b) The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

(d) ... the Escrow Fund shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for all Losses up to the Escrow Amount ($16,125,000). Claims ... in excess of the Escrow Amount may be pursued directly against Seller, subject in all cases to the Indemnification Cap ...

(e) The amount of any Losses ... shall be reduced by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received ... Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to recover under applicable insurance policies ...''',
'''Replace Sections 9.04(b), 9.04(d), and 9.04(e) with:

“(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Environmental Representations, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, shall not exceed Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), equal to 12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value (the ‘General Cap’). The General Cap shall not apply to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which is an independent obligation in addition to the General Cap.

(d) Escrow as Source of Recovery; No Limitation. The Escrow Fund is a source of security and recovery and is not a limitation on Buyer’s indemnification rights. For non-Fundamental Representation claims, the Escrow Fund shall be the first source of recovery up to the Escrow Amount. If Losses exceed the then-available Escrow Fund, Buyer may pursue Seller directly for the excess, subject only to the applicable limitations in this Article IX. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be supported by a designated portion of the Escrow Fund of not less than $1,500,000, held until thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, without limiting Buyer’s right to pursue Seller directly for any excess or after release of that designated portion, in each case through the Special Indemnity survival period.

(e) Insurance. Losses shall be reduced only by insurance proceeds actually received and finally retained by the applicable Buyer Indemnitee with respect to the same Loss, net of reasonable costs of collection and any directly attributable increase in premiums. The existence, availability, limits, exclusions, or potential recovery under any insurance policy, including any R&W Insurance Policy or environmental insurance policy, shall not limit Seller’s indemnification obligations, delay payment, or require Buyer to commence or maintain litigation against an insurer. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to seek available insurance proceeds, but shall not be required to compromise coverage rights or accept an insurer’s denial of coverage.”''',
'''The cap must be corrected to $26.875M. The seller’s escrow language is directionally consistent with the Term Sheet on excess claims, but it should expressly say escrow is not a cap and should preserve direct recovery after the fund is exhausted. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must be outside both the basket and the General Cap, with at least $1.5M held in escrow for 36 months. An “actual proceeds received” offset is acceptable only if it does not turn uncertain environmental or R&W coverage into a reduction of Seller’s primary obligation.''',
'Term Sheet §§4, 8 and 9; Playbook §§5.1, 5.4 and 6; DD Memo §III.C')

'''Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.''',

100:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** The target is itself an environmental-services business. A blanket carve-out for industry conditions and Environmental Law changes could exclude from the MAE analysis precisely the risks most relevant to the Company's value and operating model. Source: Term Sheet §12 (MAE closing condition); Playbook §2.1; Partner Instructions ¶1.
112:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The seller draft deviates from an express, binding economic term. The agreed cap is 12.5% × \$215,000,000 = \$26,875,000; the proposed \$43,000,000 cap is 20% and is not a drafting discretion point. The R&W policy does not justify reducing or changing the SPA cap structure; the SPA must conform to the Term Sheet. Source: Term Sheet §8 (General Indemnification Cap); Term Sheet §18(iv); Playbook §§5.1 and 14.
128:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** The proposed covenant would handcuff Buyer's platform integration and operational judgment through December 31, 2026, and create litigation exposure over ordinary-course decisions. The Term Sheet expressly requires only the narrow "primary purpose" negative covenant and disclaims affirmative operating obligations. The proposed replacement preserves a bad-faith manipulation protection without requiring Buyer to maximize an earnout or maintain the pre-Closing business model. Source: Term Sheet §5 (Earnout Covenant); Playbook §7.2; Partner Instructions ¶3.
142:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The current definition includes some agreed exclusions but does not expressly address Buyer-directed integration/restructuring costs, unhistorical corporate allocations, intercompany charges, or the disclosed \$1.6M affiliate lease. A precise definition is required to implement the Term Sheet and the Playbook's anti-manipulation guidance while preserving Buyer's operating flexibility. The affiliate-lease add-back should be confirmed against the final fair-market-rent analysis before signing. Source: Term Sheet §5 (Adjusted EBITDA); Playbook §7.1; DD Memo §VIII (Additional Recommendations); Schedule 4.21.
162:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The seller draft confirms current permits and policy limits but does not address change-of-control requirements, permit good standing, or facts that could lead to revocation/suspension. The DD Memo identifies 23 permits across OR, WA, CA and NV and specifically warns that state agencies may require notification or approval even in a stock deal. The insurance language should also capture the absence of cancellation/non-renewal/coverage defenses for the Hargrove project and general EIL program. Source: Playbook §§12.1 and 13.2; DD Memo §§V and VII; Schedule 4.15(b), Schedule 4.17.
185:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** The current representations address contract existence and general compliance but omit the precise risks identified by diligence: termination/non-renewal, ownership-change notices, FAR Part 42 novation, and denial risk. The four contracts represent a material revenue and backlog stream. The added representations allocate risk and create a clean basis for the covenants and conditions below. Source: DD Memo §§VI.A--C; Playbook §12.2; Term Sheet §7 (government-contract representations).
201:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The existing disclosure of affiliate arrangements is not a substitute for an interim covenant. The affiliate lease carries \$1.6M of annual rent and is relevant to Adjusted EBITDA; the seller should not be able to expand, amend, extend or terminate affiliate arrangements during the interim period without Buyer's consent. This is an express Playbook checklist item. Source: Playbook §3.2 and §14(2); DD Memo §VIII; Schedule 4.21.
223:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** A general consent clause is insufficient for federal government contracts. The DD Memo identifies the Anti-Assignment Act and FAR 42.12, with potential contract termination if required novations are not obtained. The recommended structure requires pre-Closing submission and best efforts but avoids making full agency completion an absolute condition given 60--120+ day agency timelines; it preserves a post-Closing cooperation tail. Partner/client should decide whether to elevate receipt of written "no denial/no termination" confirmations to a hard condition. Source: DD Memo §VI; Playbook §12.2; Partner Instructions ¶4.
243:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The stock structure does not eliminate change-of-control risk. The DD Memo identifies state-specific requirements in Oregon, Washington, California and Nevada and recommends both pre- and post-Closing cooperation for at least 12 months. This provision should be paired with the Section 7.02 closing protection below for permits requiring prior approval. Source: DD Memo §V.B; Playbook §§12.1 and 13.2; Partner Instructions ¶10.
261:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The current five-year, nationwide, "any business" prohibition is materially broader than the binding Term Sheet, would sweep in Seller's construction and timber operations, and creates enforceability risk. The buyer markup tracks the agreed 3-year / four-state / business-scope limitations and uses the Term Sheet's 2-year employee non-solicit. Customer/supplier non-solicitation is not included in the proposed language because it is not in the binding Term Sheet and the partner instructions direct exact conformity. Source: Term Sheet §11 and §18(v); Playbook §10.1; Partner Instructions ¶12.
283:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** "At or promptly following" Closing is insufficient for lender diligence and may leave liens or the \$28M senior loan, \$9.8M equipment financing, or \$4.5M seller note outstanding. The Term Sheet requires payoff letters at least three Business Days before Closing, simultaneous payoff through the closing funds flow, and a Buyer closing condition. The buyer may waive the condition or delay Closing, but should not be deemed to have waived it by proceeding absent an express written waiver. Source: Term Sheet §6; Playbook §9.2; Partner Instructions ¶9.
303:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** The seller draft's generic Schedule 4.05 condition does not protect the four material Government Contracts or the 23-permit portfolio. The recommended condition is a balanced position: require submission and no adverse agency action, rather than absolute completion of all novations, because agency timing may exceed the Outside Date. The environmental no-new-claims and insurance conditions are required sector-specific protections under the Playbook. Source: DD Memo §§V, VI and VII; Playbook §§12.1, 12.2, 13.1 and 13.2; Partner Instructions ¶4.
317:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The Term Sheet identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters and the Playbook treats a bound R&W policy as a standard Buyer closing condition when Buyer is obtaining R&W Insurance. The condition should not be subject to Seller approval or become a financing condition; it simply confirms the agreed risk-transfer structure. Source: Term Sheet §10; Playbook §13.1(l) and §8.2.
333:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The draft's 12-month blanket survival conflicts with the Term Sheet's 18-month general period and the Playbook's 36-month minimum for environmental representations. Dalton Creek may not crystallize within 12 months, and Hargrove remediation continues 18--24+ months post-Closing. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall apply whether or not the applicable Loss constitutes a breach of any representation or warranty and shall include all reasonable attorneys' fees, consultants' fees, investigation costs, and costs of enforcing this Section 9.02(e)."\
347:> Schedule 9.02(e) --- Scheduled Environmental Matter: Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, Oregon; EPA CERCLA §104(e) information request concerning former Company operations and waste disposal activities; estimated exposure \$1,500,000--\$6,000,000; regulatory reference number: none provided as of the date of this Agreement."
349:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** This is a required deal term, not a minor drafting point. The Dalton Creek matter is a known, disclosed environmental liability with a \$1.5M--\$6M estimated range and a long-tail CERCLA risk. Because it is disclosed, it may not support a general rep claim; it therefore needs a standalone indemnity covering investigation, defense, remediation, response costs and enforcement, with no dependence on breach, schedule disclosure, or ultimate PRP designation. Source: Term Sheet §9; Playbook §6; DD Memo §§III.A--C and VIII; Partner Instructions ¶7.
365:> "(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Environmental Representations, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, shall not exceed Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$26,875,000), equal to 12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value (the 'General Cap'). The General Cap shall not apply to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which is an independent obligation in addition to the General Cap.\
367:> (d) Escrow as Source of Recovery; No Limitation. The Escrow Fund is a source of security and recovery and is not a limitation on Buyer's indemnification rights. For non-Fundamental Representation claims, the Escrow Fund shall be the first source of recovery up to the Escrow Amount. If Losses exceed the then-available Escrow Fund, Buyer may pursue Seller directly for the excess, subject only to the applicable limitations in this Article IX. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be supported by a designated portion of the Escrow Fund of not less than \$1,500,000, held until thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, without limiting Buyer's right to pursue Seller directly for any excess or after release of that designated portion, in each case through the Special Indemnity survival period.\
371:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The cap must be corrected to \$26.875M. The seller's escrow language is directionally consistent with the Term Sheet on excess claims, but it should expressly say escrow is not a cap and should preserve direct recovery after the fund is exhausted. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must be outside both the basket and the General Cap, with at least \$1.5M held in escrow for 36 months. An "actual proceeds received" offset is acceptable only if it does not turn uncertain environmental or R&W coverage into a reduction of Seller's primary obligation. Source: Term Sheet §§4, 8 and 9; Playbook §§5.1, 5.4 and 6; DD Memo §III.C.
373:### **17. Section 9.06 --- replace anti-sandbagging with affirmative pro-sandbagging**
385:> **Track-changes comment --- CRITICAL:** The existing provision is an express anti-sandbagging clause and must be deleted. Buyer's extensive diligence---including identification of Dalton Creek---cannot eliminate the negotiated contractual allocation of risk. The Playbook requires an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause, and contractual clarity is important under Delaware law. Source: Playbook §5.3; Partner Instructions ¶2.
401:> (b) Fundamental and Special Indemnity Release. The portion of the Escrow Fund allocated to claims based on Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be held until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less amounts reserved for pending and unresolved claims properly asserted before that date. Upon final resolution of a reserved claim, the Escrow Agent shall release to Buyer the amount finally determined payable and to Seller any excess reserve.\
403:> (c) No Limitation on Direct Recovery. Release of any portion of the Escrow Fund shall not limit Buyer's right to pursue Seller directly for any Losses recoverable under this Agreement, including Losses under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, through the applicable survival period."\
405:> Conform Exhibit A to state that the Escrow Agreement shall hold not less than \$1,500,000 for the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity until 36 months after Closing and shall include joint instructions, a final non-appealable court order or arbitration award mechanism for disputed releases, and commercially reasonable investment parameters."
407:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The seller draft protects only Fundamental Representation reserves through 36 months and omits the Special Indemnity. The Term Sheet and Playbook require the Special Indemnity escrow to be held through 36 months, while the underlying Special Indemnity survives 72 months. Exhibit A is currently only a summary and should be finalized concurrently with the SPA. Source: Term Sheet §4; Playbook §5.4 and §6; DD Memo §III.C.
423:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The Term Sheet identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters and requires a fraud-only subrogation waiver. The Playbook treats this as a standard protection for the seller and should be inserted even though the seller draft is silent. The covenant should not expand Buyer's obligations beyond causing the waiver to be included in the policy. Source: Term Sheet §10; Playbook §8.2; Partner Instructions ¶11.
433:### **20. Dalton Creek diligence inconsistencies --- confirm before finalizing Schedule 9.02(e)**
437:> Seller's Schedule 4.15(d) / 4.19 describes the Dalton Creek Site as located in Lane County, Oregon and says the EPA information request is dated June 12, 2025. The Environmental DD Memo describes the site as in Clackamas County and refers to a February 12, 2025 information request.
441:> Before execution, confirm the correct site location, EPA Region 10 reference/proceeding number (if any), date of the §104(e) information request, and the final exposure estimate. Use the confirmed information in Schedule 9.02(e). Pending confirmation, define the matter by "the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility in Oregon" and the EPA CERCLA §104(e) information request concerning the Company's former operations and waste-disposal activities, without repeating a disputed county or date.
443:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The discrepancy is material because the Special Indemnity must identify the scheduled environmental matter with enough specificity to avoid a later scope dispute. It does not justify delaying the buyer markup; it does require confirmation before the SPA and schedules are finalized. Source: DD Memo §§III.A--C; Seller Schedule 4.15(d) and Schedule 4.19.
459:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The DD Memo identifies 12 PE-licensed employees as critical to permit compliance and permitted operations. The seller draft's current Knowledge-qualified representation does not address known departure risk or identify permit dependencies. This is a risk-allocation and integration item rather than a core Term Sheet deviation, so it is secondary to the Special Indemnity and permit covenants. Source: DD Memo §V.A and §VIII (Additional Recommendations).

481:2.  Correct the cap to \$26,875,000 and confirm the escrow mechanics, including a \$1.5M+ Dalton Creek allocation held through 36 months and direct recovery beyond escrow.

'''(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.''',
'''Replace Section 9.01(b) with:

“(b) All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations and the Environmental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire, except with respect to claims properly asserted in accordance with Section 9.05 before expiration. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival through the full applicable statute of limitations for environmental claims.”''',
'''The draft’s 12-month blanket survival conflicts with the Term Sheet’s 18-month general period and the Playbook’s 36-month minimum for environmental representations. Dalton Creek may not crystallize within 12 months, and Hargrove remediation continues 18–24+ months post-Closing. The opening position should be full applicable limitations period; the instructed drafting assumption is 36 months, with the longer alternative flagged for Marcus and the partner.''',
'Term Sheet §8 (Survival Periods); Playbook §4.2; DD Memo §III.C; Partner Instructions ¶6')

348: Schedule 9.02(e) — Scheduled Environmental Matter: Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, Oregon; EPA CERCLA §104(e) information request concerning former Company operations and waste disposal activities; estimated exposure $1,500,000–$6,000,000; regulatory reference number: none provided as of the date of this Agreement.”''',
349: '''This is a required deal term, not a minor drafting point. The Dalton Creek matter is a known, disclosed environmental liability with a $1.5M–$6M estimated range and a long-tail CERCLA risk. Because it is disclosed, it may not support a general rep claim; it therefore needs a standalone indemnity covering investigation, defense, remediation, response costs and enforcement, with no dependence on breach, schedule disclosure, or ultimate PRP designation.''',

352: add_issue(doc,'16. Section 9.04 — cap, escrow and insurance mechanics','HIGH',
353: '''(b) The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.
354: 
355: (d) ... the Escrow Fund shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for all Losses up to the Escrow Amount ($16,125,000). Claims ... in excess of the Escrow Amount may be pursued directly against Seller, subject in all cases to the Indemnification Cap ...
356: 
357: (e) The amount of any Losses ... shall be reduced by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received ... Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to recover under applicable insurance policies ...''',
358: '''Replace Sections 9.04(b), 9.04(d), and 9.04(e) with:
359: 
360: “(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Environmental Representations, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, shall not exceed Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), equal to 12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value (the ‘General Cap’). The General Cap shall not apply to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which is an independent obligation in addition to the General Cap.
361: 
362: (d) Escrow as Source of Recovery; No Limitation. The Escrow Fund is a source of security and recovery and is not a limitation on Buyer’s indemnification rights. For non-Fundamental Representation claims, the Escrow Fund shall be the first source of recovery up to the Escrow Amount. If Losses exceed the then-available Escrow Fund, Buyer may pursue Seller directly for the excess, subject only to the applicable limitations in this Article IX. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be supported by a designated portion of the Escrow Fund of not less than $1,500,000, held until thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, without limiting Buyer’s right to pursue Seller directly for any excess or after release of that designated portion, in each case through the Special Indemnity survival period.
363: 
364: (e) Insurance. Losses shall be reduced only by insurance proceeds actually received and finally retained by the applicable Buyer Indemnitee with respect to the same Loss, net of reasonable costs of collection and any directly attributable increase in premiums. The existence, availability, limits, exclusions, or potential recovery under any insurance policy, including any R&W Insurance Policy or environmental insurance policy, shall not limit Seller’s indemnification obligations, delay payment, or require Buyer to commence or maintain litigation against an insurer. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to seek available insurance proceeds, but shall not be required to compromise coverage rights or accept an insurer’s denial of coverage.”''',
365: '''The cap must be corrected to $26.875M. The seller’s escrow language is directionally consistent with the Term Sheet on excess claims, but it should expressly say escrow is not a cap and should preserve direct recovery after the fund is exhausted. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must be outside both the basket and the General Cap, with at least $1.5M held in escrow for 36 months. An “actual proceeds received” offset is acceptable only if it does not turn uncertain environmental or R&W coverage into a reduction of Seller’s primary obligation.''',
366: 'Term Sheet §§4, 8 and 9; Playbook §§5.1, 5.4 and 6; DD Memo §III.C')

369: '''Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.''',
370: '''Replace Section 9.06 in its entirety with:
371: 
372: “Section 9.06 Pro-Sandbagging. The right to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any knowledge acquired (or capable of being acquired) by Buyer or any of its Representatives at any time, whether before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any such representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. No claim for indemnification under this Article IX shall be defeated, diminished, or otherwise affected by reason of any investigation, knowledge, or notice of Buyer or any of its Representatives, regardless of whether such investigation, knowledge, or notice was obtained before or after the Closing.”''',
373: '''The existing provision is an express anti-sandbagging clause and must be deleted. Buyer’s extensive diligence—including identification of Dalton Creek—cannot eliminate the negotiated contractual allocation of risk. The Playbook requires an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause, and contractual clarity is important under Delaware law.''',
374: 'Playbook §5.3; Partner Instructions ¶2')

add_issue(doc,'16. Section 9.04 — cap, escrow and insurance mechanics','HIGH',

'''(b) The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

(d) ... the Escrow Fund shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for all Losses up to the Escrow Amount ($16,125,000). Claims ... in excess of the Escrow Amount may be pursued directly against Seller, subject in all cases to the Indemnification Cap ...

(e) The amount of any Losses ... shall be reduced by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received ... Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to recover under applicable insurance policies ...''',
'''Replace Sections 9.04(b), 9.04(d), and 9.04(e) with:

“(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations, Environmental Representations, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, shall not exceed Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), equal to 12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value (the ‘General Cap’). The General Cap shall not apply to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which is an independent obligation in addition to the General Cap.

(d) Escrow as Source of Recovery; No Limitation. The Escrow Fund is a source of security and recovery and is not a limitation on Buyer’s indemnification rights. For non-Fundamental Representation claims, the Escrow Fund shall be the first source of recovery up to the Escrow Amount. If Losses exceed the then-available Escrow Fund, Buyer may pursue Seller directly for the excess, subject only to the applicable limitations in this Article IX. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be supported by a designated portion of the Escrow Fund of not less than $1,500,000, held until thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, without limiting Buyer’s right to pursue Seller directly for any excess or after release of that designated portion, in each case through the Special Indemnity survival period.

(e) Insurance. Losses shall be reduced only by insurance proceeds actually received and finally retained by the applicable Buyer Indemnitee with respect to the same Loss, net of reasonable costs of collection and any directly attributable increase in premiums. The existence, availability, limits, exclusions, or potential recovery under any insurance policy, including any R&W Insurance Policy or environmental insurance policy, shall not limit Seller’s indemnification obligations, delay payment, or require Buyer to commence or maintain litigation against an insurer. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to seek available insurance proceeds, but shall not be required to compromise coverage rights or accept an insurer’s denial of coverage.”''',

'''The cap must be corrected to $26.875M. The seller’s escrow language is directionally consistent with the Term Sheet on excess claims, but it should expressly say escrow is not a cap and should preserve direct recovery after the fund is exhausted. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must be outside both the basket and the General Cap, with at least $1.5M held in escrow for 36 months. An “actual proceeds received” offset is acceptable only if it does not turn uncertain environmental or R&W coverage into a reduction of Seller’s primary obligation.''',
'Term Sheet §§4, 8 and 9; Playbook §§5.1, 5.4 and 6; DD Memo §III.C')
add_issue(doc,'17. Section 9.06 — replace anti-sandbagging with affirmative pro-sandbagging','CRITICAL',

'''Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.''',
'''Replace Section 9.06 in its entirety with:

“Section 9.06 Pro-Sandbagging. The right to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any knowledge acquired (or capable of being acquired) by Buyer or any of its Representatives at any time, whether before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any such representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. No claim for indemnification under this Article IX shall be defeated, diminished, or otherwise affected by reason of any investigation, knowledge, or notice of Buyer or any of its Representatives, regardless of whether such investigation, knowledge, or notice was obtained before or after the Closing.”''',

'''The existing provision is an express anti-sandbagging clause and must be deleted. Buyer’s extensive diligence—including identification of Dalton Creek—cannot eliminate the negotiated contractual allocation of risk. The Playbook requires an affirmative pro-sandbagging clause, and contractual clarity is important under Delaware law.''',
'Playbook §5.3; Partner Instructions ¶2')

61:  **Critical**      Article IX --- new                   No Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.                                                           Add 72-month, dollar-one, outside-general-cap indemnity; hold \$1.5M+ in escrow through 36 months.
333:> "(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity set forth in Section 9.02(e) shall survive the Closing for seventy-two (72) months following the Closing Date, and any claim properly asserted in accordance with Section 9.05 before expiration shall survive until finally resolved."
337:### **15. New Section 9.02(e) --- Dalton Creek Special Indemnity**
347:> "(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the EPA information request under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company's former operations at the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility in Oregon, (ii) any investigation, inquiry, claim, notice of potential responsibility, designation as a potentially responsible party, enforcement action, administrative order, consent decree, lawsuit, contribution claim, or other proceeding relating to the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, and (iii) any contamination, release, threatened release, response cost, remediation obligation, natural resource damage, property damage, bodily injury, defense cost, settlement, judgment, penalty, fine, or other liability arising from or relating to the Company's operations, transportation, arranging for disposal, or disposal of Hazardous Substances at or in connection with the Dalton Creek Disposal Facility, whether arising under CERCLA, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Oregon Environmental Cleanup Law, or any other applicable Law. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall apply whether or not the applicable Loss constitutes a breach of any representation or warranty and shall include all reasonable attorneys' fees, consultants' fees, investigation costs, and costs of enforcing this Section 9.02(e)."\
365:> Replace Sections 9.04(a), 9.04(b), 9.04(d), and 9.04(e) with:\
367:> "(a) Basket. Seller shall not be obligated to indemnify any Buyer Indemnitee for Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, until the aggregate amount of such Losses exceeds the Basket Amount (\$2,150,000), and then only for Losses in excess of the Basket Amount. The Basket Amount shall operate as a true deductible and not as a tipping or first-dollar basket.\
369:> (b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, shall not exceed Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$26,875,000), equal to 12.5% of the Base Enterprise Value (the 'General Cap'). The General Cap shall not apply to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, which is an independent obligation in addition to the General Cap.\
371:> (d) Escrow as Source of Recovery; No Limitation. The Escrow Fund is a source of security and recovery and is not a limitation on Buyer's indemnification rights. For non-Fundamental Representation claims, the Escrow Fund shall be the first source of recovery up to the Escrow Amount. If Losses exceed the then-available Escrow Fund, Buyer may pursue Seller directly for the excess, subject only to the applicable limitations in this Article IX. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be supported by a designated portion of the Escrow Fund of not less than \$1,500,000, held until thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, without limiting Buyer's right to pursue Seller directly for any excess or after release of that designated portion, in each case through the Special Indemnity survival period.\
375:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The cap must be corrected to \$26.875M. The seller's escrow language is directionally consistent with the Term Sheet on excess claims, but it should expressly say escrow is not a cap and should preserve direct recovery after the fund is exhausted. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity must be outside both the basket and the General Cap, with at least \$1.5M held in escrow for 36 months. An "actual proceeds received" offset is acceptable only if it does not turn uncertain environmental or R&W coverage into a reduction of Seller's primary obligation. Source: Term Sheet §§4, 8 and 9; Playbook §§5.1, 5.4 and 6; DD Memo §III.C.
391:### **18. Section 9.08 and Exhibit A --- preserve Special Indemnity escrow through 36 months**
405:> (b) Fundamental and Special Indemnity Release. The portion of the Escrow Fund allocated to claims based on Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be held until the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less amounts reserved for pending and unresolved claims properly asserted before that date. Upon final resolution of a reserved claim, the Escrow Agent shall release to Buyer the amount finally determined payable and to Seller any excess reserve.\
407:> (c) No Limitation on Direct Recovery. Release of any portion of the Escrow Fund shall not limit Buyer's right to pursue Seller directly for any Losses recoverable under this Agreement, including Losses under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, through the applicable survival period."\
409:> Conform Exhibit A to state that the Escrow Agreement shall hold not less than \$1,500,000 for the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity until 36 months after Closing and shall include joint instructions, a final non-appealable court order or arbitration award mechanism for disputed releases, and commercially reasonable investment parameters."
411:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The seller draft protects only Fundamental Representation reserves through 36 months and omits the Special Indemnity. The Term Sheet and Playbook require the Special Indemnity escrow to be held through 36 months, while the underlying Special Indemnity survives 72 months. Exhibit A is currently only a summary and should be finalized concurrently with the SPA. Source: Term Sheet §4; Playbook §5.4 and §6; DD Memo §III.C.
447:> **Track-changes comment --- HIGH:** The discrepancy is material because the Special Indemnity must identify the scheduled environmental matter with enough specificity to avoid a later scope dispute. It does not justify delaying the buyer markup; it does require confirmation before the SPA and schedules are finalized. Source: DD Memo §§III.A--C; Seller Schedule 4.15(d) and Schedule 4.19.
463:> **Track-changes comment --- MEDIUM:** The DD Memo identifies 12 PE-licensed employees as critical to permit compliance and permitted operations. The seller draft's current Knowledge-qualified representation does not address known departure risk or identify permit dependencies. This is a risk-allocation and integration item rather than a core Term Sheet deviation, so it is secondary to the Special Indemnity and permit covenants. Source: DD Memo §V.A and §VIII (Additional Recommendations).
477:- Escrow amount and general 18-month release are consistent with the Term Sheet; markup is limited to clarification that escrow is not a recovery cap and to the required 36-month Special Indemnity holdback.
